label: Glassflow
Colour

Colour source *Feeds every tinted surface. Container colour is read from the tab itself, so tabs in different containers differ. Tabs with no container fall back to whatever you pick below. Favicon is not offered: Zen exposes no CSS variable for it.*
Fallback when the source is unavailable *Used when a tab has no container, no folder, or the workspace has no colour assigned. This is why some tabs looked untinted before.*
Custom colour *Used when the source or fallback above is set to Custom. Any CSS colour: hex, rgb(), hsl(), oklch().*
Darkness *Mixes the source toward black before anything uses it. 0% keeps Zen's raw hue, which tends pastel. 25% is noticeably deeper, 45% approaches a jewel tone.*
Second gradient colour *Used by any gradient whose end mode is set to 'Fade to a second colour'. Ignored otherwise.*
Selected tab
Style selected tabs *Independent switch. Every option below applies only to this state.*
Tint strength *How much of the source colour this state carries, as a percentage. This is the gradient's starting value.*
Opacity *Fades the whole tab including label and favicon. 1 is fully opaque.*
Gradient direction *Independent of every other state, so unloaded tabs can run the opposite way from selected ones.*

Gradient end *What the gradient fades toward. Transparent shows whatever is behind the tab. Weaker tint keeps the same hue at lower strength. Second colour blends toward the Second gradient colour set above.*

options.label: Fade to a weaker tint of the same colour

label: End tint strength *Only used by 'Fade to a weaker tint' and 'Fade to a second colour'. Expressed as a percentage of the source colour, so 40% of a 42% start lands near 17%.*
Gradient spread *Where the end stop lands, as a percentage across the tab. 100% spans edge to edge. Lower values finish the fade early and leave a flat run after it.*
Glass sheen *The specular highlight band. Direction and strength come from the Glass section.*
Glass rim *A 1px inner highlight along the top edge. The difference between glassy and merely translucent.*
Outer glow *A soft tinted halo around the tab. Replaces the rim shadow, so it includes the rim when both are on.*
Frosted blur *One compositor pass per tab in this state. The most expensive option in the mod. Only blurs what the browser painted, so over a flat sidebar there is little to work with.*
Blur strength *Only applies when frosted blur is on for this state.*

Shared glass

Glass intensity *Scales every sheen, rim and glow alpha at once. 0 removes the glass look and leaves flat tint. Per-state switches decide where glass appears; this decides how strong it is. A multiplier on alpha, so it costs nothing at any value.*
Sheen direction *Which way the specular band runs. Separate from each state's tint gradient direction.*
Tab roundness *Corner radius for tab backgrounds. Arc rebinds Zen's --border-radius-medium to its own setting; this overrides it for tabs only.*
Texture *An overlay pattern on every tab state. All options are plain CSS gradients, so the cost is one extra background layer and nothing else.*
Tab strip

Gradient across the whole tab strip *A wash behind every tab spanning the full strip rather than each tab individually. Also gives frosted blur something with structure to work against. Uses the workspace colour, since container colour only exists per tab.*
Strip gradient strength *How strong the wash is at its top.*
Accent bar on the selected tab *A 3px coloured bar down the left edge. The clearest marker if you keep tints subtle. Uses the same layer as Arc's container glow, so it replaces it.*

Hide Arc's container glow *Arc paints a blurred bar of container colour across the left half of every container tab. With Zen forcing a container per workspace that lands on every tab, and it is usually the extra colour on the left.*
Window buttons
Enable macOS-style traffic lights *Replaces the window controls with round glass buttons. Turn OFF Arc 2.0's own 'macOS style buttons' first.*
Position *Which end of the sidebar row the buttons sit on.*
Show colour at rest *Off: neutral grey until hovered.*
Stretch into a vertical oval on hover *Only the button under the cursor stretches.*
Oval height multiplier *Multiple of the diameter. 1.0 stays circular, 1.3 is a soft oval.*
Show glyphs on hover *Triggered by hovering anywhere in the group, matching macOS.*
Glyph size *How much of the button the mark fills. Above 85% it touches the rim.*
Button opacity *Fades buttons at rest. Hover always restores full opacity.*
Glass sheen on buttons *Independent of the tab sheen switches.*
Glass rim on buttons *Independent of the tab rim switches.*
Frosted blur on buttons *Cheap here: three small elements, not one per tab.*
Close colour *Alpha below about 0.7 reads as glass. Hover stacks a second pass to deepen the hue.*
Minimise colour *Keep alpha below about 0.7.*
Maximise colour *Keep alpha below about 0.7.*
Diameter *macOS uses 12px, Arc uses 14px.*
Gap between buttons *macOS uses roughly 8px.*
Folders and groups
Enable folder styling *Restyles group labels and bodies. Advanced Tab Groups keeps ownership of folder behaviour; this only changes appearance.*
Folder roundness *Corner radius for group labels and bodies.*
Folder tint *How much of the group's own colour the label carries.*
Folder gradient direction *Independent of every tab state.*
Glass sheen on folder labels *Independent of the tab sheen switches.*
Glass rim on folder labels *Independent of the tab rim switches.*
Tint the expanded folder body *A soft fade behind the tabs inside an open folder.*
Hide Arc's folder bar *Arc draws a vertical bar via tab-group-container::after.*
Sidebar
Enable sidebar styling *Tints the sidebar background. Arc's compact sidebar opacity still applies underneath; set that first, then use this for the tint on top.*
Sidebar tint *How much workspace colour the sidebar carries.*
Sidebar opacity *Fades the whole tinted layer.*
Sidebar gradient direction *Independent of every other section.*
Glass sheen on the sidebar *Independent switch.*
Glass rim on the sidebar *Independent switch.*
Frosted blur on the sidebar *A second blur pass on top of whatever Arc, Transparent Zen or DWMBlurGlass already apply. Stacking blurs rarely composes well.*
Sidebar blur strength *Only applies when sidebar blur is on.*
Troubleshooting
Outline every element Glassflow touches *Magenta on tabs, cyan on window buttons, lime on folder labels, orange on the sidebar. No outline means Glassflow is not matching that element.*
